Definitions, metadata gaps & provenance

    Every observation is one supplied seed-row return at one perturbation level. Episode count and aggregation are unreported. R₀ is the median non-robust return from a documented pure-axis nominal column, checked for exact agreement across all pure-axis nominal vectors. Normalized retention is Z = R / R₀; reliability S(t) = fraction of supplied seed rows with Z ≥ t. Clipped AUC = mean clip(Z, 0, 1). Low-return fraction uses Z < 0.5; this is not a physical failure or success rate.

    Pure-axis level 0 is excluded from shifted summaries. Compound level 0 is included because its fixed background is already perturbed. Within each axis, levels have equal weight; summaries give each received axis equal weight. Lowest-20% return averages the six lowest of thirty seed rows separately at each condition, then averages conditions and axes. This is not the lower tail of a matched cross-axis policy score. Quantiles use linear interpolation. SD uses n − 1.

    Row numbering is source order, not authenticated training-seed IDs. No across-method paired differences, cross-axis seed trajectories, bootstrap intervals, significance, noninferiority or L1/L2/L3 certificates are inferred. Results cover only the received folders; the remaining data is not present. Same-named TV/KL labels in different folders are not certified identical configurations.

    Severity AUC is the trapezoidal return average over the observed shifted magnitude interval, then averaged equally across axes. It differs from reliability AUC, which integrates over return thresholds. Worst-condition mean is the minimum of condition means, not a matched-policy worst-case score. No unobserved severity range is extrapolated.
